string-array.name: hints
string-array.item: Did you read the tutorial? (\"$ tutorial\")
Did you know that you can easily switch your theme? Have a look at the cmd \"$ theme\"
Did you know? You can create your custom theme and share it with other users. Have a look at the cmd \"$ theme -create\"
Doubts about a command? Use \"$ help cmdName\"
Did you know? You can listen to music using HelCLI. Have a look at the cmd \"$ music\"
Did you know? HelCLI 6.4 introduced App Groups.\nYou can get more details with the cmd \"$ apps -tutorial\"
Did you know? You can see your notifications inside HelCLI. If you\'re interested, have a look at the tutorial: \"$ notifications -tutorial\"
Are you sick of clearing your screen? Have a look at the options \"clear_after_cmds\", \"clear_after_seconds\" and \"maxlines\"
Do you want to use your wallpaper as HelCLI background? Use the cmd: \"$ config -set system_wallpaper true\"
Doubts about any config option? Use the cmd \"$ config -info [option]\"table
Did you know that HelCLI supports aliases? For more info, use the cmd \"$ alias -tutorial\"
Did you know? You can exclude an unwanted notification by long-clicking on it
You can disable this messages with the cmd \"$ config -set show_hints false\"

string-array.name: tutorial
string-array.item: Use the command \"help\" to get a list of available commands
If you want to get info about the behavior of a command, type \"help cmdName\"
Launch your apps typing their name
You can call your contacts with the cmd \"call contactName\"
HelCLI is highly customizable. Check \"config -ls\" or use the cmd \"config -tutorial\" to see what you can change
Browse the theme gallery with \"theme -list\", then try one with \"theme -preview [name]\" and \"theme -apply [name]\"

Print the list of commands, or info about a command 

Usage: 
help [command] 

Example: 
$ help exit
This file is too big, consider opening it with an other text editor
Bluetooth is not available on this device
Command not found.\nTry to use \"$ help\" or \"$ tutorial\"
write your SMS or nothing to cancel

-add [aliasName] [alias content] -> add a new alias 
-rm [aliasName] -> remove an existing alias 
-ls -> list your aliases 
-file -> open alias.xml

-ls -> list your apps 
-lsh -> list your hidden apps 
-show [appName] -> re-show an hidden app 
-hide [appName] -> hide an app 
-l [appName] -> show details about an app 
-ps [appName] -> show Google Play Store page for an app 
-st [appName] -> show Settings details for an app 
-default_app [index] [appName or most_used or null] -> set the default_app at the specified index 
-frc [appName] -> force HelCLI to launch an app 
-file -> open apps.xml 
-reset [appName] -> reset the "launched_times" value of the given app to 0 
-mkgp [groupName] -> create a new group with the given name 
-rmgp [groupName] -> delete the group with the given name 
-gpcolor [groupName] [color] -> set the color for the given group 
-addtogp [groupName] [appName] -> add the given app to the given group 
-rmfromgp [groupName] [appName] -> remove the given app from the given group 
-lsgp [OPTIONAL: groupName] -> list your groups, or list the content of the given group
Set the brightness of your device \n$ brightness [0-100]

Perform basic operations (+ - * / % ^ sqrt) 
Example: 

$ calc 4+2-5 
1 

$ calc 2 ^ (2*2) 
16 

$ calc sqrt25 
5
Show the changelog of the current version

-set [option] [value] -> set the value of an option 
-append [option] [value] -> append the given string to the value of the selected option 
-edit [file] -> edit a config file inside HelCLI (theme.xml, ui.xml, behavior.xml, ...) 
-file [file] -> open a config file with another app 
-erase [option] -> set the value of an option to "" 
-setr [option] [value] -> same to "-set", but restarts HelCLI automatically 
-get [option] -> get the value of an option 
-fontsize [value] -> change the global font size 
-reset [option] -> reset the value of an option 
-info [option] -> request info about the given option 
-apply [file] -> move a file to the HelCLI directory 
-tutorial -> open the tutorial page
Offer a coffee to the developer (PayPal only)

Print the available commands, or info about a command 

Usage: 
$ help [command]

Extract text from HTML pages 
-query [filter ID] [optional: format ID] [URL] -> parse the specified XPath entry with the specified URL 
-add [type] [ID] [expression] -> add a new expression of the given type (json, xpath or format) 
-rm [ID] -> remove an existing expression 
-edit [ID] [expression] -> change an existing expression 
-ls [type] -> shows the expressions of the given type 
-tutorial -> show the tutorial on GitHub 
-file -> open the file htmlextract.xml

-next -> play the next song 
-previous -> play the previous song 
-play -> play/pause the player 
-stop -> stop the player 
-ls -> list your tracks 
-select [song] -> play the selected song 
-info -> get info about the current song 
-seekto [seconds] -> seek to the selected part of the current song

-add [optional: lock {true/false}] [text] -> add a new note 
-rm [row] OR [text] -> remove an existing note 
-cp [row] OR [text] -> copy an existing note to clipboard 
-ls -> list all your notes 
-clear -> remove all notes (except the locked ones) 
-lock [id] OR [text] -> lock an existing note 
-unlock [id] OR [text] -> unlock an existing note 
-tutorial -> open the tutorial page on GitHub
Leave a feedback on the Play Store page
-add [ID] [regex] -> add a new regex with the given ID \n-rm [ID] -> remove the regex with the given ID \n-test [ID] [string] -> test the corresponding regex over the given string

-to [ID or packageName] [what] -> reply to the last notification from the application bound with the given ID 
-bind [appName] -> bind the application 
-unbind [appName] -> unbind the application 
-ls -> show your bound applications 
-check [ID or packageName] -> check the last notification from the application bound with the given ID 
-tutorial -> open the tutorial page on GitHub
Restart HelCLI and load modified values

-gg [search this...] -> Google Search 
-ps [search this...] -> Google Play Store 
-u [URL] -> open the URL 
-yt [search this...] -> YouTube 
-dd [search this...] -> DuckDuck Go

-ls [appName] -> show the shortcuts of this app \n-use [shortcutID OR shortcut index] [optional: appName] -> use the specified shortcut \n-cp [index] [appName] -> copy to clipboard the nth shortcut of the selected app (first: 0)
Get info about battery charge, wifi status and mobile data

Browse, apply and share themes 

-list -> show every theme in the gallery 
-preview [name] -> see what a theme looks like before applying it 
-apply [name] -> apply a theme (a name from -list, or a https:// link to a theme file) 
-import -> pick a theme file (.json) on your phone and apply it 
-import [https://link] -> download a theme file, save it and apply it 
-export [name] -> save your current colors as a theme 
-share [name] -> send a theme file to another app 
-delete [name] -> delete a theme you saved or imported 
-set [element] [color] -> manually set one color (#RRGGBB or #AARRGGBB) 
-preset [name] -> same as -apply 
-old -> go back to the theme you had before 
-standard -> go back to the default colors

Print the current time with the given format 

Usage: 
$ time [index] (index means the index of the desired time_format

-rm -> uninstall HelCLI 
-about -> show info about the developer and the current version 
-reset -> removes the HelCLI folder and resets default settings (restart required) 
-log [fileName] -> log the text on screen to the file 
-priority [command] [int] -> set the priority of the selected command 
-sourcecode -> open the GitHub page 
-folder -> print the path of the HelCLI folder
-add [line] [text] -> add a new note at the specified line (the note will be appended if line is omitted) \n-rm [line] -> remove the note at the specified line \n-clear -> remove all the notes
Open the tutorial page on GitHub

Make your device vibrate. 

Usage: 
$ vibrate [milliseconds] 
$ vibrate [pattern: wait, vibrate, wait, vibrate, wait, ...] 

Example: 
$ vibrate 300 
$ vibrate 0,300,500,300

-set [stream] [volume: 0-100] -> set the volume for the selected stream 
-profile [mode] -> set the profile mode 
-get [stream] -> get info about the selected stream 

stream: 
	* voice call -> 0 
	* system -> 1 
	* ringer -> 2 
	* media -> 3 
	* alarm -> 4 
	* notificaton -> 5 

mode: 
	* silent -> 0 
	* vibrate -> 1 
	* normal -> 2

Pull your HelCLI settings from a folder in a public GitHub repository. 
Edit the files on GitHub, then run git pull on the phone. 

-remote [owner/repo/folder] -> choose where to pull from (also owner/repo/folder@branch, or a github.com link) 
-pull -> apply the newest settings from the remote and reload 
-status -> show the remote and the last pull 
-undo -> put back the settings from before the last pull 

Files it understands: theme.xml, ui.xml, behavior.xml, suggestions.xml, toolbar.xml, cmd.xml (only the settings they contain are changed), alias.txt, and themes/*.json

Show your Claude usage at the top of the home screen. 

Plan limits (claude.ai Pro/Max): the 5-hour and weekly %. A small script on the computer where you use Claude Code publishes them; see tools/claude-usage in the HelCLI repo. 
API spend: this month's Claude API cost, from Anthropic's usage and cost API (needs an Admin API key from an organization). 

-show / -hide -> show or hide the line 
-plan [user/gist_id] -> where your plan limits are published (-plan off to stop) 
-key -> save the Admin API key you copied to the clipboard 
-forget -> delete the saved Admin API key 
-budget [dollars] -> monthly API budget, to show a % (0 = none) 
-update -> refresh now 
-status -> what's set up 

Change the text with the claude_format setting (behavior.xml).

A breakdown of the phone's memory: in use, cached (freed when apps need it), free, and swap. 

Usage: 
$ ram 

Android doesn't let apps see how much memory other apps use, so there's no per-app list.

A breakdown of storage: apps, images, videos, audio, other files, system, free space, and SD cards. 

Usage: 
$ storage -> overview and the 5 biggest apps 
$ storage apps -> the 20 biggest apps (storage apps all: every app) 
$ storage cache -> apps with the most cache, which is safe to clear (storage cache all: every app) 
$ storage access -> give HelCLI Usage access, which Android needs for app sizes and the image/video/audio split

A summary of the phone, neofetch style: Android version, model, uptime, theme, CPU, RAM, storage and battery, with the theme's colors. 

Usage: 
$ sysinfo

Your calendar agenda, from every calendar on the phone. Asks for calendar access the first time. 

Usage: 
$ cal -> today and the next 6 days 
$ cal today 
$ cal tomorrow 
$ cal 14 -> the next 14 days (up to 60)

Network details: WiFi or mobile, signal, addresses, gateway, DNS, and whether the internet is working. 

Usage: 
$ ip 
$ ip public -> the address the internet sees (asks api.ipify.org)

Checks whether a host answers, and how fast. 

Usage: 
$ ping -> checks your router, then the internet (finds out whether a problem is the WiFi or beyond) 
$ ping [host] -> e.g. ping github.com

Looks up a name: its addresses, how long the lookup took and which DNS server answered. Give an IP address to find its name. 

Usage: 
$ dns [host] -> e.g. dns github.com

Runs a HelCLI command later. 

Usage: 
$ at 22:00 theme -apply oled -> today at 22:00 (tomorrow if that's passed) 
$ at 7:30pm flash, at 7pm ... -> 12-hour times work too 
$ at +30m vibrate 500, at 2h ..., at 1h30m ... -> from now 
$ at daily 7am cal today -> every day 
$ at -> list the jobs 
$ at cancel [number] -> cancel one; at clear -> cancel all 
$ at exact -> let jobs run on time (Android 12+)

Draws a QR code you can scan with another phone's camera. 

Usage: 
$ qr [text] -> e.g. qr https://github.com/Garza304/HelCLI 
$ qr -> the text you copied 

Up to about 100 characters fit on the screen. For WiFi: qr WIFI:T:WPA;S:network name;P:password;;

Ask Claude a question; the answer appears in the terminal. Follow-up questions remember the conversation. 

Usage: 
$ ask [question] -> e.g. ask how do I find my phone's IP address? 
$ ask -new -> start a new conversation (it also resets after 30 minutes) 
$ ask -key -> save the Claude API key you copied (from the clipboard) 
$ ask -forget -> delete the key from HelCLI 

Needs a Claude API key from platform.claude.com, and Android 8 or later. Each question costs a little on that account. 
Settings: ask_model (default claude-opus-5-5) and ask_effort (default low) in behavior.xml.

Weather comes from Open-Meteo: free, and no key or account needed. 

-update -> update the weather now 
-enable -> show the weather 
-disable -> hide the weather 
-location [place] -> a city (Berlin, or San Antonio, Texas), coordinates (lat,lon), or auto to use the phone's location 
-tutorial -> open the weather help page

-inc [appName] -> include an application 
-exc [appName] -> exclude an application 
-color [color] [appName] -> set the color to be used for the application 
-format [ID] [appName] -> apply the format with the given ID to the corresponding application 
-add_filter [ID] [filter] -> create a new filter with the given ID 
-add_format [ID] [format] -> create a new format with the given ID 
-rm_filter [ID] -> delete the filter having the given ID 
-rm_format [ID] -> delete the format having the given ID 
-access -> show the system settings page dedicated to the Notification Access 
-file -> open notifications.xml 
-tutorial -> show the tutorial page

-ls -> list your contacts 
-l [contactName] -> show details about a contact 
-add -> create a new contact 
-edit [contactName] -> edit an existing contact 
-rm [contactName] -> remove a contact
Close HelCLI and reset the default launcher

-add [ID] [update_time_in_seconds] [url] -> add a new RSS feed. HelCLI will try to get new contents every [update_time_in_seconds] seconds 
-rm [ID] -> remove this RSS feed 
-ls -> list your RSS feeds 
-l [ID] -> show the whole content of the corresponding RSS feed 
-show [ID] [boolean] -> toggle the [show] property of the given saved RSS feed 
-update_time [ID] [update_time_in_seconds] -> set the update time of the corresponding RSS feed 
-format [ID] [format] -> set the format of the corresponding RSS feed ([format] can be both a string or the ID of an existing format) 
-color [ID] [color] -> set the base color of the corresponding RSS feed 
-wifi_only [ID] [boolean] -> if [boolean] is true, the corresponding feed will be updated only if your device is connected to a WiFi network 
-last_check [ID] -> show the last time HelCLI checked this RSS feed 
-entry_tag [ID] -> set the base tag for every single entry (default: "item") 
-date_tag [ID] [tag] -> set the tag which holds info about the publication date (default: "pubDate") 
-add_command [ID] [IDs (comma separated)] [regex] [cmd] -> create a new regex command that will be applied on the RSS feeds corresponding to IDs 
-rm_command [ID] -> rm the corresponding regex command 
-frc [ID] -> update the corresponding RSS feed 
-info [ID] -> show info about the corresponding RSS feed settings 
-include_if_matches [ID] [regex] -> if the given regex matches on an RSS feed item, it will be shown ([regex] can be both a string or the ID of a regex saved inside regex.xml) 
-exclude_if_matches [ID] [regex] -> if the given regex matches on an RSS feed item, it won't be shown ([regex] can be both a string or the ID of a regex saved inside regex.xml) 
-add_format [ID] [format] -> create a new format that you will be able to use for more than one RSS feed 
-rm_format [ID] [format] -> remove an existing format 
-file -> open the file rss.xml
Interrupt the current shell process and create a new one
Change the username and device name: username [new_user] [new_device]
-install -> download and setup BusyBox\n-remove -> uninstall BusyBox
